claude.result:
Done. `game.html` (78 KB, ~1720 lines) is written to the working directory — a complete, self-contained ASHFALL OUTPOST with all 13 systems from the brief and no TODOs. The `result.json` and `stderr.log` files in the directory pre-existed; I created only `game.html` (a temporary verification script was created and removed).

What's implemented:

- **Core loop** — single state object, mulberry32 PRNG stepped from a serialized `rngState` (seed 1337, editable; no `Math.random` anywhere), with the fixed turn order documented in the header comment and the Dev tab: storm → production (in chain order) → needs → arrivals → events → trade → caps/win check.
- **Map & economy** — 8×8 seeded terrain (ash/rock/water/vent/ruins), 14 building types with terrain requirements and adjacency bonuses shown in tooltips, and real chains: ash→soil→food (sifter/composter/greenhouse, consuming water) and ore→metal→parts (mine/forge/workshop, consuming power). Storage caps with logged overflow.
- **People & needs** — named colonists with 4 jobs, skill 1–5 that grows with use, fatigue, and morale; shortages degrade morale visibly and recoverably, with strikes and departures at zero.
- **Research, events, trade, storms** — 10-node tree with prereqs and locked/available/done states; 12 weighted events (6 with real choices) on 8-turn cooldowns; a periodic caravan with drift + scarcity pricing and limited stock/scrip; escalating ashstorms mitigated by two research nodes and storm walls, repaired with parts plus idle labor.
- **Save/load, endings, UI, Dev** — JSON textarea save/load with validation errors; win/lose/"never thrived" at turn 60 with a scored breakdown and endless mode; 6 tabs, Space/1–6 keys, custom hover-and-tap tooltips explaining every number, mobile-friendly at 360px; Dev panel with 20 invariant assertions and a 200-turn greedy-policy benchmark run twice to prove hash-identical determinism.

One honest caveat: this environment blocked all script execution (`node`/`python` require an approval no one could grant, including with the sandbox override), so I could not run the headless verification I built. Instead I re-read the entire file line by line and fixed the one weakness found (a flaky formulation of the event-cooldown test). The first things to do when you open it: click **Dev → Run Tests** and **Run Benchmark** — they were designed to be the executable proof I couldn't run here.
